# FontFreeze

> FontFreeze is a free, open-source web app that freezes OpenType features and variable font axes into a new font file. It lets you permanently enable or disable features such as stylistic sets (ss01-ss20), character variants (cv01-cv99), ligatures (calt, liga), slashed zero (zero) and old-style figures (onum), or turn a variable font into a static instance, so the customized font works in apps that don't support font feature settings. It runs entirely in the browser (fonttools on Pyodide/WebAssembly); font files are never uploaded.

App URL: https://mutsuntsai.github.io/fontfreeze/

## Typical questions FontFreeze answers

- How do I make a font's ss01 / cv01 / zero feature the default, permanently?
- How do I use stylistic sets or character variants in Visual Studio, Microsoft Word, a terminal, or any app that only lets me choose a font family?
- How do I permanently disable programming ligatures in Fira Code, JetBrains Mono, Cascadia Code, etc.? (Deactivate `calt`, and `liga` if present.)
- How do I convert a variable font into a static TTF at a specific weight or width?
- How do I subset a font, or rename its family so it can be installed alongside the original?

## How to use

1. Open a TTF/OTF font file (or drop it on the page, or select an installed local font).
2. For variable fonts, choose a predefined instance or set each axis value.
3. In the feature list, mark features as activated or deactivated (leave blank to keep default behavior).
4. Optionally subset glyphs, rename the family (a "Freeze" suffix is added by default), and choose TTF or WOFF2 output.
5. Click "Generate font!", download, and install the font.

## How it works

Deactivated features have their lookups removed. Activated features have their lookups moved into `calt` (or `rvrn`, configurable), which is on by default in most environments. Single-glyph substitutions can additionally be applied directly to the character map for maximum compatibility.
